transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, hi. Thanks. I guess what really brought me in is... my wife, mostly. She gets pretty frustrated with me lately. Like, she’ll be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or when he needs rides. He’s been needing a lot of rides lately because his truck finally broke down last month. It’s an old Ford, and I told him the alternator was going bad—you can just hear that high-pitched whining sound, you know? I used to work on cars a bit back in the day, so I know what to listen for. But he wouldn't take it in, and now it's sitting in his driveway. So anyway, my wife will be going over his schedule with me, and I’m looking right at her, but then a minute later I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. It just sort of slips right past me.
Did you have similar troubles with paying attention or staying focused back when you were a child?

Well, yeah, I guess so. Even way back in grade school, you know, definitely before I was 12, my teachers used to tell my parents that I was a bright kid, but I was always daydreaming. And I'd always leave my homework stuffed inside my desk. 

Man, remember those old wooden desks with the tops that lifted up on those squeaky hinges? They had that little groove for your pencil at the top. I used to keep all sorts of junk in there. I had this huge collection of Hot Wheels cars I'd hide in the back of it. The old Redline ones, you know? I had this metallic blue Camaro that was just... it was my absolute favorite. I traded a kid named Jimmy for it at recess one day, gave him two of my duplicate Mustangs for it. Jimmy moved away in fifth grade, actually, went out to Ohio... 

Wait, what was I talking about? Oh, right, my teachers. Yeah, they were always having to come over and remind me to finish my classwork because I'd just be off in my own world instead of doing the assignment.

Anxious? No, not really. I'm a pretty laid-back guy, honestly. I don't sit around chewing my nails or anything like that. I mean, my wife worries enough for the both of us, especially about the house and the yard. 

Actually, the only thing that really gets me worked up lately is this mole problem we have in the backyard. Or maybe it's gophers? Whatever they are, they are just absolutely tearing up the tomato plants. I spent all day Tuesday trying to put up this wire mesh—chicken wire, you know? But you have to bury it at least two feet down or the little guys just tunnel right under it. It’s a whole process. I was actually down at the hardware store looking for the right gauge of wire, the galvanized kind so it doesn't rust out in the wet soil over the winter, and I ran into this guy I used to work with, Bob. Bob had this crazy story about his boat engine, he was trying to rebuild the carburetor on this old pontoon he bought off Craigslist... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, worrying. But yeah, no, I don't really have a problem with anxiety or anything like that.

{"intent": "Assess for hyperactivity and motor restlessness to distinguish between hyperkinetic disorder subtypes", "question": "Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or like

Restless? No, not really. I don't feel like I have to be moving all the time or anything like that. I can sit still for hours, honestly. 

Especially if I'm in my favorite chair. It's this big brown leather La-Z-Boy, and my wife absolutely hates it because she says it throws off the whole look of the living room, but I refuse to get rid of it. I found it at that huge furniture warehouse out on Route 9—you know the one? They always have that giant inflatable gorilla on the roof during their President's Day sales. Anyway, the lever on the side gets a little stuck sometimes, you gotta really yank it backward to get the footrest to pop up, but once you're settled in, it's just incredibly comfortable. Our dog, Buster, he's a golden retriever mix, and he knows exactly when I'm about to sit down. He’ll actually trot over and try to beat me to it. He’s getting a bit of arthritis in his back hips now, poor guy, so I usually just let him have the footrest once I get it up... 

Wait, what did you ask me originally? Oh, right, fidgeting. Yeah, no, I don't really do that. I'm perfectly fine just sitting in one spot.
Do you often find yourself blurting out answers before questions are completed, or having difficulty waiting your turn to speak?

Blurting things out? No, I don't think so. I'm usually pretty quiet in conversations, honestly. I just let the other person talk. 

Like our mailman, Gary. He's a good guy, but man, he can really talk your ear off. He was standing on the porch for a solid twenty minutes yesterday telling me all about his daughter's wedding up in Portland. Portland, Maine, not Oregon. My wife and I actually took a trip up to Maine back in... oh, it must have been '98. We rented this little A-frame cabin right on the water. Ate lobster practically every single night. You know, the locals up there tell you the trick to boiling lobster is to put a little fresh seaweed right in the pot, it gives it that real authentic ocean flavor. We even bought a big blue enamel pot at a yard sale up there just to bring home, but I think it's been sitting in the basement for twenty years now... 

Wait, sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, right, interrupting people. But yeah, no, I don't really have a problem waiting my turn to speak. I just kind of hang back and listen.

{"intent": "Determine whether the patient had symptoms of hyperactivity during childhood to differentiate between hyperkinetic disorder (F90.0) and attention deficit disorder without hyperactivity (F9

Hyperactive? When I was a kid? No, I don't think so. I was actually a pretty quiet kid, mostly just kept to myself. I wasn't bouncing off the walls or anything like that. 

I used to spend hours in my room just building those balsa wood model airplanes. You remember those? The kits where you had to pin all the fragile little pieces to a board over the blueprints and glue them together. The glue had this incredibly strong smell, and my mother absolutely hated it. She was always opening the windows, even in the dead of winter. We grew up just outside of Chicago, so opening a bedroom window in January was basically freezing the whole house out. But my dad and I built this huge B-17 bomber once. Took us maybe three weeks of working on it every night. We painted it olive drab, put all the little star decals on it, the whole nine yards. We finally took it down to the park to fly it, and on the very first throw, a gust of wind caught it and lodged it right at the top of this massive oak tree near the duck pond. Those ducks were mean, by the way. If you didn't have pieces of bread for them, they would literally chase you down the sidewalk... 

Wait, sorry, I'm rambling again. What were we talking about? Oh, right, being hyper as a kid. But yeah, no, I was perfectly happy just sitting still for hours working on my models.
